### 7.3 Iterating

- **One class at a time** (Alex, 2026-10-29: "你一类一类改，快速迭代然后测regression"). Count the misses by mechanism; take the largest
  class; trace it to the sentence that causes it; change one thing aimed at that class; run the whole bench (a prompt change alters every
  request) against the previous version; read every regression to its raw answer. The pages that showed the failure locate its
  mechanism; only the whole bench (every set, every draw) accepts the change.
- **Name the effect on the judgement first.** Every proposed change states the effect it is expected to have on a reader or on the final
  judgement, and is tested there where possible; a step's own counts do not decide it alone. A fix that keeps moving its error to
  neighbouring cases stops being tuned on that set (Alex, 2026-11-09: "感觉现在一直在修一些mknor的原地打转，你是不是要思考下现在具体还差什么high priority big impact 的需要做？";
  he approved this rule the same day, D391).
- **A model call is a sampler.** Re-send a stored request before calling its answer a defect. Totals and acceptance come from at least
  three samples beside a fresh control; a bar the control fails against itself judges nothing. A direct-read pass
  (one send per article, every answer read beside its source; D238) locates mechanisms; its counts are one draw and are labelled so.
- **A written log.** One row per arm: hypothesis, change, numbers against the control (regressions first), kept or not. Refuted arms and
  your own mistakes stay in it; the next session starts from its last row.
- **Own the loop, within what Alex agreed.** When the direction is agreed and no stop is in force (`CURRENT_STATE.md`), push your own
  hypotheses through $0 checks and probes of a few cents on stored cases without asking. A registered test, an end-to-end run, or
  anything that departs from the agreed plan starts on his word; a result that contradicts the hypothesis stops the line and goes to him
  (D355: "如果有什么不符合hypothesis 的地方你需要终止然后和我说我们重新评估"). While he is not active (D439), "his word" is the council's
  recorded consensus, and a stopped line goes to the council for re-assessment.
- **Council before every change is sent.** A prompt, schema, code or criterion change, including one found by reading a probe, is a new
  arm. It goes to an independent Codex read and a challenge round before its first send, and its result goes to a challenge round
  before the next change. Reading the traces and the model's own account locates a fix; it does not review it (Alex, 2026-11-08:
  "你这些改动有我你有好好的跑council 再下手").
  Every round's reasoning and decisions are reflected on in the council until there is a consensus; the decision is recorded, and
  the next test goes straight ahead, held to the PRD and its quantified goals, with every trace read by you yourself and not only
  by readers (Alex, 2026-11-10: "你应该跑council loop 来reflect 你每一轮的思路还有决策，需要你打成共识，记录决策，向前直行测试。不要drift,我们有PRD和量化目标，
  你自己作为llm 下去看所有trace").
- **Small first, then one run.** A hypothesis is first validated the simplest way, on a few stored cases and a few cents, and shown to
  work at a high level before any full analysis or stability test is built (Alex, 2026-11-04: "don't overspend resources on wasting time.
  We need to validate the hypothesis in a very simple way and to make sure that it works on a high level before we dive into do the full
  analysis stability test. This is a principle you should remember"). A day or week slice before any whole-corpus run; preflight on
  stored data before any paid run (§5); no edit while a run is live (§9). A paid run measures a configuration; it never tries a fix.
  Before each send, write what it can still change in the decision and which risk the cheaper check left uncovered; a replicate or
  control that only re-measures noise or a settled comparison is not sent, and a fix is not sent before the model's own account and the
  request locate where the decision is made (Alex, 2026-10-30: "你跑这么多次真的有意义吗"; "我感觉你在为了跑而跑"). Several fixes on one
  base are each proved on stored data in minutes and then run together once (Alex, 2026-11-02: "快速验证。不要drift,不要跑超级繁琐的全方位验证，先poc 改，能work,有结论，全部改动放到一起再跑完整"; D266).
- **One recommendation, one test.** What reaches Alex as the next step of work is one recommendation and one test of it, reached after
  rounds of review (Claude's own, Codex's, an independent reader's) on the traces until a round finds nothing serious; never a menu of
  arms or options, never a conclusion the next probe overturns (a choice that changes what the system does still goes to him with its
  options and a recommendation, Authority and scope) (Alex, 2026-11-04: "就测试一种，一次 … 你就没有自己看5轮review，能不能自己有个超级自信的定论和证据再给我提建议？").
  An agreed recommendation is first challenged by an independent reader on the concrete evidence behind it ("why you give
  recommendations for this. What did you see exactly?"). A review round reads a rule as its author meant it; only a send shows how the
  model applies it: before a registered test, the changed request is sent on the cases that motivated it, a few cents.
- **A failed arm is diagnosed before the next one.** When an arm fixes its class and regresses another, write the root cause first: the
  process error (what grew, what the small sample did not guard) and the mechanism, traced to the raw answers and the model's account,
  never a guess stated as the cause. A small sample guards every class the change can move, not only its own. When a fix keeps moving
  another class, the call is doing several jobs: move the rule to its owner (a field's definition sits in the schema beside the field)
  rather than add a sentence (Alex, 2026-10-30: "那你这些修改都是失败的呀，为什么，根因，你要检讨然后再接着尝试。我觉得你已经陷入deep loop 了").
  A failed step of a plan is fixed and re-run at that same step: its failures are the work list, and nothing later in the plan and no
  substitute plan starts before it passes (Alex, 2026-11-04: "你为什么要drift? 你现在明明还有这么多的问题要fix,你到底知不知道你要fix什么？").
  Before a fix is proposed, write which goal the mechanism still serves and what the product already gives for it; a measurement that
  removes the reason a mechanism exists retires the mechanism instead of starting its repair (Alex, 2026-11-04: "I told you to think about
  it and you're giving me suggestions that you reject yourself").
- **Before a version is rejected, the rejection is checked.** Every failed or refused answer behind a "did not pass" is read against its
  source and put down as the model's error or the measuring rule's or check's error; a rule or check that refuses right answers is fixed,
  and a version that already meets the goal (what it was built to fix is fixed, nothing that was right turned wrong) is not dropped for a
  stricter rule a later review added. Alex, 2026-11-05: "你到底是不是再搬石头砸自己的脚？各种reject自己，你确定是正确的rejection 吗？你又下去看trace吗？";
  "你不能每次都这样判错然后浪费我时间，我需要你深度看完所有失败trace给我准信下一步你要跑什么才能收敛".
- **Correct, then cheap.** Make the pipeline right and stable before any cost, speed or throughput work; report cost as a baseline only
  (Alex, 2026-10-25).

## 8. Product thinking

- Think like a hedge-fund analyst. A thesis is an argued view about the business and the world; its stance comes from the argument
  weighed against what is priced. Extract the few metrics or segments that carry it; financial-statement lines are its evidence, never its
  definition.
- **Lean cautious, catch the increment.** Most of what an item says is noise: not everything is evidence and not everything is a lead. A
  typical claim or background line is common knowledge (what an analyst following the company knew before the item) and is not kept
  without a number and a specific narrative; new information that changes an answer is never missed. Alex, 2026-10-29 (D243):
  "不是什么事情都是惊弓之鸟需要抽取，杂音还是很大的，我们整体应该倾向谨慎不要看什么都是线索的感觉，但是同时我们要敏感一些新的信息带来的增量不要错过".
- **A senior analyst's granularity.** A question is a bet an analyst would hold a card for: a big matter, never trivia (a deal, product or
  project opens one only when its scale can change revenue, profit, cash or credit risk). Small matters open no question, and whether
  their statements are kept follows the evidence rule; wordings, deadlines, milestones and periods of one bet are one question, and a
  statement carried by several outlets is one statement (how code applies it: §3, Identity). Two questions stay apart only when their answers can move apart and an analyst
  would bet on each separately (D248). Alex, 2026-10-30: "我觉得核心就是这个颗粒度的把控要符合一个高端的hedge fund analyst 的思维。不要搜集一堆鸡毛蒜皮的事情，要看重要的大事，合并整合关键的信息，这个是这个步骤的原则".
- The extraction standard (§7.1, piece 1) is the step's standard. Its two sources are applied before designing a prompt, evaluation or
  change (D228): the thesis library's four evidence tiers (`docs/prd/06-views.md`, Four evidence tiers) and the investment-question
  reasoning in the 90-thesis review (`research_notes/对冲基金论点粒度与金标/codex-challenger.md`, section 1; research, not a replacement for
  recorded decisions). Source type and what a claim can support are separate judgments; no tier has a fixed score. Ask what revenue,
  profitability, cash risk or competitive position the information can change; then separately decide whether it supports an existing
  question or merits a new one. Indirect, incomplete and forecast information is evidence under the routing rules; none of those
  properties, nor an inability to open a new question, alone makes it worthless.
- Evaluate the overall research judgment against the source, the existing question and the evidence. Gold examples teach the reasoning
  and its boundaries; reasonable alternative wording, evidence strength and inference are allowed (D226, D228). Record material factual
  errors, unsupported assumptions and downstream losses separately. Do not turn a review's questions, output labels or optional details
  into an automatic all-or-nothing score. Missing market expectations or historical context means that aspect was not tested, not that
  it passed or failed.
- When a thesis-quality check fails, look first at the unit of thought (are these the arguments that move the stock?), not deeper into
  the numbers. Numbers are verified by code where they exist.
- Outcomes are tracked and shown, never a gate on what a view may say. Missing data is "no data to verify", never a pass or a fail. A
  repeat is not new evidence, and model agreement is not corroboration.

## 9. Workspace and operations

- Inspect a path before writing to it; new stored data gets a new, dated name; chain guarded steps with `&&`. Deleting stored data needs
  Alex's request, a backup, exactly identified items and a log entry.
- Absolute paths. Commands run under zsh: pass a list as an array. No foreground `sleep`.
- Preserve existing and concurrent changes: never reset, clean or stash work that is not yours. Never run parallel agents that edit
  shared modules.
- When Alex names a step, the test is that step alone through its own harness (extraction: stored requests re-sent, answers sifted,
  scored against the gold). A full-pipeline run, a registered test, or a paid send beyond the probes of a few cents an agreed direction

## 1. Goal (end to end)

Each question's judgement must receive the facts that can change its answer; facts that no question receives, those that bear on no question, must
not be piled into some one question. What is measured is the final judgement (the frozen judgement ruler, reader B, at the window end 2026-07-14), not
any one step's own score.

## 2. The core blocker (proven)

**The system uses a fact for a question only when the fact "states exactly this question's own figure". An analyst also reasons onward from a fact: the other party's figure in a deal, price and volume for a product's revenue, a product's variants for its launch, and so on. The filing step cannot do this; the judging step reasons onward once it has the facts.**

This one blocker has two faces (described earlier as "two problems"):

- **The parking lot.** Filing does not recognise facts that bear on a question indirectly, so no question takes them; yet to be kept, a fact must
  first be filed (D209, D264). So D273 added the fallback sentence, which parks them in NVIDIA's total-revenue question. Of the reports under the
  total-revenue question, in the part the gold read, 32–39% are ones the standard does not keep, 31–44% are kept but used by none of the 22 questions,
  and only 7–10% are what the gold actually uses to judge total revenue (three draws); 24–44% of the total-revenue question's judgement citations are
  news about other companies or the whole market (Intel graphics-card retail prices, a gas-fired power plant in Taiwan).
- **Narrow questions starve.** Questions that only indirect facts can answer do not receive them: the custom-chip question received none of Broadcom's
  figures in any of the three draws, and judged "below $40 billion" in all three; the operating-margin and NVIDIA capital-spending questions received
  nothing at all and were never judged.

## 6. How to measure (the ruler does not move; the method does not change again)

- **Requests**: rebuild each stored request byte for byte with the production code, changing only the one place that holds the filing rule; the
  rebuilt request's archive id must equal the original's, or it is not sent (`resend_filing.py`, AGENTS §5). Never re-send the archive's copy whose
  keys were sorted alphabetically.
- **Articles**: development set = the 54 articles of `selection.json` (already read many times); held-out set = articles the extraction gold read and
  the judgement gold uses that are not among those 54, drawn once before the test, with the list frozen and never changed afterwards. Both sets are
  measured and reported apart.
- **Control**: the unchanged requests re-sent 3 times the same day. No comparison with the archive (model drift).
- **Each answer**: goes through the production code checks and filing first (including "keep only the narrowest" and "no home means dropped"), and is
  counted after.
- **What is counted** (`measure_filing.py`, with its matching rule fixed: items are matched on the distinct numbers and the proper nouns other than
  NVIDIA in the source text; a source passage the system quotes that overlaps the gold's passage also counts as the same matter; "optional" counts as
  optional; the citations in the body of the gold's answers are read):
  - whether each fact that matters (one the gold uses to judge any question) reached the question that uses it, counted per fact, not per "fact ×
    question";
  - per question: the facts that matter that reached it and the new noise that appeared, counted by the decision rule below;
  - the parking lot: how many facts the total-revenue question (v1, together with v22) takes in, and what they are;
  - noise: how many of the sentences the standard does not keep are kept; per question, how noise is filed (links on facts the standard does not keep
    or no question uses);
  - how many core and supporting facts appear; the facts that matter that are dropped; how many questions each fact is filed under on average.
  - Matching still has a small error (spot check: the new rule mismatches a few and misses a few); say so when reporting the numbers, and read the
    ones that matter one by one.
- **Decision rule** (rewritten on 2026-11-04 with Alex's agreement, D360. The original draft required "every draw above the highest of the control's
  three" and the like, which the control itself fails when measured again, so it cannot tell good from bad. Script `decide.py`; written down and frozen
  before each test; each draw's numbers and the totals are all reported):
  - **Totals, with luck ruled out first**: each article's 6 answers from the new and the old arm are randomly reassigned between the two arms 4,000
    times (with a fixed random seed); the new rule's difference counts as a real change only when fewer than 5% of the reassignments reach it.
    - Development set: facts that matter reaching the question that uses them must rise; the count under the total-revenue questions (v1, v22) must
      fall; sentences the standard does not keep must not rise; core facts must not fall.
    - Held-out set: facts that matter reaching the question that uses them must not fall; sentences the standard does not keep must not rise; core
      facts must not fall.
  - **Per question, counted by code against the gold** (development and held-out sets together):
    - A fact that matters which reaches the question at least two fewer times under the new rule than under the control counts as "one fewer" for that
      question; in under the control all three times and under the new rule none of the three, it counts as "lost outright". A move to another question
      that the gold also uses it for and that is no broader than the original (one home per fact, D207) does not count as fewer; a move to a broader
      question counts. "One more" in the opposite direction offsets it.
    - A noise sentence (not kept by the standard, or kept but used by no question) that the new rule files under the question at least twice while the
      control never does counts as "new noise"; filed all three times, it counts as "outright new noise". The opposite direction offsets it.
    - Any question with a net 3 fewer, a net 2 lost outright, a net 5 more new noise, or a net 3 more outright new noise fails. These thresholds are the
      smallest values that keep "misjudged when new and old are exactly the same" within about one in ten; at the test, first compute the
      misjudgement rate from the reassignments; if it is above one in ten, raise the threshold most prone to misjudgement by one step, then compare with
      what was measured.
  - **Smaller changes** (a question 2 fewer, two or three more noise) cannot be told from luck in three measurements: all are listed, given to a reader
    who did not write the rule to read against the raw answers, and written into the report; they do not decide pass or fail.
  Only when everything passes does it become a candidate; a candidate runs end to end three times on the 14-day window (extraction re-sent, matching and
  judging run as usual, scored on the frozen judgement ruler), and that step needs Alex's word.

## 1. Step 1: statements dated after their article ($0) — the premise does not hold; nothing is built

- **Census** (`date-census.txt`): 31 statements in the six full-run draws (c1 6, c2 7, c3 6, p1 1, p2 4, p3 7) carry an original day later than
  their article's stored day. Every one read: almost all are **correct dates against a stored day that is one day early** (a Bloomberg
  Intelligence survey "released on Tuesday Jul 7" whose item is stored as 07-06 though its `published_at` is "Tue, 07 Jul 2026 07:00:00 GMT";
  Singapore's charges "(July 6)" in an item stored as 07-05; Nokia's 07-15 announcement in an item stored as 07-14); one is a page updated after
  publication (a 07-10 page holding SanDisk's results of August 5). The two "August 2026" statements both trial readers flagged quote the page
  itself ("Nvidia said in August 2026 …" in a 07-12 item): the page carries later text; the system copied it faithfully.
- **Source census** (`source-date-census.txt`, all 3,643 eligible items 2026-07-01..10-27): 165 items have a stored day earlier than the UTC
  date of their `published_at` (some by months: a `published_at` of 24 October on an item stored as 07-01, likely a feed's later date, not the

You are a senior hedge-fund analyst. A research topic was opened on the company from the item below. Write the one question the topic is judged on: what it asks, its answer ladder and its due day. The ladder is written once, from this item only, and is never rewritten. Write in English.

What the question asks
- A judged question concerns one figure for a named period or one event. Write a question, not an assertion. A figure or event must be able to determine the outcome on the due date. For a figure, the question names the period it covers or the day it is measured at, and the material that settles it.
- A topic's wording may ask about more than one thing. Judge the one the topic's outcome names as what is tracked. List every other part of the topic's wording that the question leaves out, a second figure or event, a condition or a comparison, in not_judged, each with one sentence on why it is not the one tracked. Never fold two things into one ladder: "Will the regulator approve the drug for a second use, and how many patients will take it in the first year?" is judged on the approval when that is what its outcome names, and the patient count is listed; "How much will the carrier's fuel bill be next year, and will its pilots strike?" is judged on the fuel bill when that is what its outcome names, and the strike is listed.
- Return no_ladder with the reason, and ladder null, in seven cases: the topic has no main figure or event, naming none, or naming several with none of them the main one; nothing in the topic can be checked on a date, which for an event means that neither the topic nor the item gives a date and the topic names no period, unless it is a pending regulatory decision, for which use the company's current fiscal year-end; the figure is a company's figure for a quarter or a half-year, which is evidence to a yearly question; the figure covers a period that is not one fiscal or calendar year, such as a survey's rolling twelve months, and neither the topic nor the item gives the day it is published; the figure is for a year that has already ended on the item's day; the figure is for a year beyond next year, unless the topic's opens_as is binding_obligation; or the question belongs to another company or to a matter that no theme in the request's themes covers, in which case name that company or matter in the reason. Do not rewrite a figure for a year beyond next year as an event to keep it; a numeric completion target may define the state of an event that is itself the topic.

Whose question it is
- A question about the company's revenue, profit, share, product progress or its own obligations is about the company: object is its ticker, even when policy or macroeconomics drives it. A question about what happens in the world, such as licensing, interest rates or aggregate spending, rather than the resulting effect on one company, belongs to a theme: object is a theme id from the request's themes. A question whose tracked outcome is a government's or regulator's decision to permit, restrict or ban a class of products or trade belongs to the theme that covers it, also when the product is the company's own: whether a health ministry lifts its import ban on one drug maker's vaccine belongs to the theme that covers that country's drug approvals. When the tracked outcome is the company's own sales, shipments or revenue under such a decision, the question is about the company, as is a proceeding against the company itself, such as an investigation of its conduct or a fine. A question about another company's own figure, or about a matter no listed theme covers, has no object here: return no_ladder.

The ladder
- Define concrete, verifiable conditions now. Do not write a ladder whose thresholds depend on an unspecified future target. Conditions must not overlap or leave gaps: exactly one must hold when resolved; avoid vague "partial" outcomes.
- An event is answered in event, in at most three outcomes. happened is the condition under which the event the question asks about has happened by the due day. ruled_out says who can rule the event as a whole out before the due day, and how: by_whom names the company, authority, court or party whose decision it would be; decision is one full sentence that names them and says what they decide against the event as a whole, or that they formally abandon or withdraw it, after the item's day. The due day arriving without the event is no one's decision and is never written there: it is what is left. ruled_out is null only when no one's decision can rule the event out before the due day. Write no other condition: what is left, neither of the two, needs none, and where both would hold the event counts as happened. A difference inside an outcome, such as an approval with conditions against one without, is not an outcome of its own; when the topic's wording names it, list it in not_judged. A regulator reviewing a merger gives: happened, the regulator has cleared the merger by the due day; ruled_out, by_whom the regulator or the parties to the merger, decision the regulator blocks the merger or the parties withdraw the filing. An authority's investigation or examination that the question asks to end in a published decision or conclusion always has a ruling out: happened, the authority publishes that decision or conclusion by the due day, whatever it finds; ruled_out, by_whom the authority, decision the authority formally abandons or withdraws the proceeding without it. The proceeding still going on the due day is neither, and a decision to go on with it is not a ruling out. A safety agency examining a carmaker's defect gives: happened, the agency publishes its findings; ruled_out, by_whom the agency, decision the agency formally closes or withdraws the examination without publishing any.
- A figure is answered in figure: its unit (USD, percent, count, GW, MW, TWD or multiple; other when it is none of these, the question then naming the unit), the one year it covers (written FY2027 for a company's figure, which uses its fiscal year; written 2026 for a theme's figure, which uses the calendar year) and exactly five ranges of that one figure. Each range has an inclusive lower bound lo and an exclusive upper bound hi. Money amounts are written in full (12000000000, not 12 billion); percentages use 73, not 0.73. The lowest range has lo null, the highest hi null; every other bound is a number.
- Fill exactly one of event and figure; the other is null.
- reference is what this figure or event is measured against when the topic opens, quoted in the item's own words. Its kind is expected when the item states what the market expects: a consensus, the company's guidance, the stated plan or deadline. For a figure only, when the item states no expectation and gives the amount most recently reported for the same quantity (the same thing measured the same way: not a part of it, a ceiling on it or another quantity), that amount is the reference and its kind is last_reported; a reported amount is never called an expectation. Otherwise reference is null. value is the number the item states, with value_to its upper end when the item states a range; when the item gives it in words alone, value is null: never supply a number the item does not state. The ranges of a figure state the outcome against a reference that has a value: the middle range holds that value, or runs from at or below a stated range's lower end to at or above its upper end, and the ranges on either side are outcomes above and below it. When reference is null or has no value, the ranges are your own estimate of the outcomes that could happen.
- favourable_end, for a figure about a company: higher when a higher outcome is good for its business, lower when a lower one is, with one sentence why. A result and its direction are separate: capital spending can build capacity or hurt returns. For an amount the company owes, guarantees or has committed to pay, when neither the topic nor the item settles which end is good for the business, because they argue both ends or say nothing on it, it is lower; when the topic's own words say that more of it is good, it is higher. A retailer's lease guarantees that the item says win store sites and also weigh on its credit are lower; an airline's aircraft purchase commitments that the topic tracks as the fleet growth its plan needs are higher. For a theme's figure it is n/a.

The due day
- Set the due day when the question can be resolved. It falls after the item's day, and on or after the day the material that settles the question is published.
- For a figure, use its publication date, which falls after the end of the period the figure covers: stated when the topic or the item gives it, expected_publication when you set the day you expect it to be published. Company figures use the company's fiscal year: "this year" contains the item's publication day, and "next year" follows it; convert fiscal years using the fiscal-year note. Other figures use calendar years.
- For an event, name the date at which its outcome is assessed: stated when the topic or the item gives it; period_end when it is the last day of the period the topic names, or the company's current fiscal year-end for a pending regulatory decision that has no date.
- When the topic's opens_as is binding_obligation, the due day is at most 548 days (18 months) after the item: for an obligation already taken on, its next annual filing; for one not yet signed, the day by which the signing can be checked.

item.text:
The core problem is that **the new system cannot reliably turn an important, complicated matter into a question it can actually answer**. For example, it opened cloud-company spending as one topic covering two years, then declined to answer it because neither year was identified as the main one.

This is deeper than a faulty refusal: the first step writes the topic, and the later step must turn it into one answerable question. Their rules do not yet provide a reliable way to handle a matter with several independently meaningful parts. I would treat this as the **leading explanation for the latest failure**, not as a proven explanation for every product defect. Facts failing to reach existing questions remain a separate, established problem.

The evidence carrying that conclusion is:

1. **The product goal is an answer informed by the facts that can change it.** That is the phase’s stated end-to-end goal; it is not enough for a step to keep facts or write plausible-looking questions. The same document establishes an earlier filing failure in the old system: indirect facts were missed, while the judge could reason from them when shown them. That is measured evidence for the old path, not proof that every failure in the new path has the same cause. [Filing phase, §§1–2](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/prd/10-filing-phase.md)

2. **The latest week shows the problem directly.** One run opened 13 topics; the answer-writing step declined 9 of 39 attempts across four topics. Both spending topics covering two years were declined in all three attempts. The matching and judge were not run, so the effect on final answers was not measured. The view that cloud spending deserved a question is a reader’s judgement. [Second-week result](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/second-week/RESULT.md)

3. **The refusal is partly the agreed design working as written.** Alex chose to judge the main part and decline a topic with no main part; the cost of leaving two real bets unanswered was recorded as an open defect. He also chose to keep two sides of the same bet together. Those choices do not establish how to handle two separately tracked years. This is a design boundary, not evidence that the model simply ignored an instruction. [D397 and D436](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md)

4. **The problem recurs, but its size is not a general rate.** Across stored material, six topics whose question asked two things were declined in all three attempts. A separate boundary study identified cloud spending and a memory price as two worthwhile matters lost outright; other cases were disputed or judged not worth opening. These include repeated news and different readings. [Result](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/second-week/RESULT.md), [boundary study](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/second-week/NO-MAIN-BOUNDARY-STUDY.md)

5. **Other faults are real and prevent a clean pass.** Agreed errors include a question that lost the guarantee’s name and omitted parts that should be shown as unjudged. Across four readings, the kinds of agreed fault changed; the record does not demonstrate one repair that removes them all. An audit also found that “the topic’s wording” is undefined in the request. This weakens any claim that multi-part topics are the sole technical cause. [Gate map](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/second-week/FIRST-GATE-MAP.md), [prompt audit](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/second-week/PROMPT-AUDIT-TWO-CLASSES.md)

6. **The new system has not shown an end-to-end win.** In the July comparison, it retained 51 of 55 decisive facts for its lost questions, yet lost those graded answers before judgement; the old system also lost at opening. The comparison was small, with unresolved reader disagreements, and does not rank the systems. [Full census](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/e2e-comparison-2026-11-13/CENSUS-FULL-RESULT.md)

**What would show I am wrong:** a source-by-source reading of the stored declined topics showing that the apparently separate parts are usually one bet, not worth tracking, or already answered adequately elsewhere. Equally, if the missing questions would not affect any useful judgement while a different recurring failure does, that failure should take priority.

**The last two days partly aimed at this, but also circled.** D466 explicitly stopped repeated sentence changes after the score did not move; D473 and D479 record further failed candidates. D483 then correctly shifted attention toward what a reader receives. The recent week and D555–D558 exposed the connection between topic shape and refusal, but the subsequent search for small fixes to separate answer-writing faults has not produced a product-relevant repair. D544 chose the new path as the direction of work, not as a demonstrated better system. [Decision log](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md)

Candidates I considered and rejected as the *one* core problem:

- **“The judge is wrong.”** The latest diagnostic did not run it; earlier evidence is insufficient to make that the main cause.
- **“Facts are not delivered.”** Confirmed in individual new-system cases, but not shown to explain the latest missing questions. [Lean log, §§11–12](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/LEAN-LOG.md)
- **“The pass rules are too strict.”** Some readings are disputed, but agreed faults remain even on the favourable reading.
- **“Just split every topic.”** The boundary study shows that this would also produce questions about matters readers judged unworthy.

**One next step:** a $0, source-by-source review of the stored declined matters, including the unworthy controls, to decide which parts an analyst would track separately and whether each could become an answerable question without creating trivia. Its falsifier is that the worthwhile multi-part matters cannot be distinguished from the controls by an independently reviewable reason. This would inform a design; it would not prove a change works.

The product choice is Alex’s: **when one important matter contains two separately tracked figures, should the product show one topic with two judged questions, open two topics, or leave it unanswered?** I recommend one topic with two judged questions when the figures are genuinely separate bets, while keeping two sides of the same bet together. That recommendation needs the stored-case review first. Finishing the latest week would test the answers that exist, but its own design says it cannot answer this missing-question issue. [Completion design](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/second-week/COMPLETION-DESIGN.md)

Position: The highest-priority unresolved problem is the handoff from an important matter to answerable questions; its full product impact remains to be established.
